title: # zia_url_categories: removing a URL from `urls` also removes `db_categorized_urls` entries in ZIA (regression from #505)

blocks.heading: # zia_url_categories: removing a URL from `urls` also removes `db_categorized_urls` entries in ZIA (regression from #505)

blocks.item: Earlier versions back to the #505 change appear to behave the same way.

blocks.text: When `urls` changes on an existing `zia_url_categories` resource, Update sends only incremental `ADD_TO_LIST` / `REMOVE_FROM_LIST` calls. Each call carries the **whole desired category**, built with `expandURLCategory(d)`. ZIA applies the action to every list in the payload, not just `urls`. As a result:

blocks.item: **Any removal from `urls`** also removes the desired `db_categorized_urls` entries from the category, even when `db_categorized_urls` is unchanged in config.
Planned changes to `db_categorized_urls` are not applied: removals never happen, and additions only happen as a side effect of `ADD_TO_LIST`.

blocks.text: The plan doesn't show any of this. After the apply, Read refreshes state from the API, and the **next** plan shows drift. Applying that second plan fixes the category, because with `urls` unchanged Update falls through to the full update (`""` action).
Start from an existing custom category:

blocks.code:
resource "zia_url_categories" "test" {
  configured_name     = "PROVIDER_BUG_REPRO"
  super_category      = "USER_DEFINED"
  type                = "URL_CATEGORY"
  custom_category     = true
  urls                = ["test.example.com"]
  db_categorized_urls = ["keep-a.example.net", "keep-b.example.net", "remove-me.example.org"]
}

blocks.text: Apply. The ZIA admin portal matches the config.
Change only the lists (the same thing happens if you leave `db_categorized_urls` untouched and only remove from `urls`):
**Expected:** Custom URLs is empty. URLs Retaining Parent Category is `keep-a.example.net`, `keep-b.example.net`.

**Actual:** Custom URLs is empty. URLs Retaining Parent Category contains **only `remove-me.example.org`**: the two entries the plan left unchanged were removed, and the one the plan removed is still there.
The next plan shows the drift, and applying it fixes the category:

The add direction (adding to `urls` and to `db_categorized_urls` together) looks fine, but only because `ADD_TO_LIST` with the full desired `db_categorized_urls` is a no-op for entries that already exist.

blocks.code:
desiredCategory := expandURLCategory(d)   // includes DBCategorizedUrls, IPRanges, keywords, ...
...
removeCategory := desiredCategory
removeCategory.Urls = urlsToRemove
UpdateURLCategories(ctx, service, id, &removeCategory, "REMOVE_FROM_LIST")
...
addCategory := desiredCategory
addCategory.Urls = urlsToAdd
UpdateURLCategories(ctx, service, id, &addCategory, "ADD_TO_LIST")

blocks.text: The full update (`""` action) only runs when there are no `urls` changes. So in the remove case, `DBCategorizedUrls` (and presumably `IPRanges`, `IpRangesRetainingParentCategory`, `Keywords`, `KeywordsRetainingParentCategory`) goes out with `REMOVE_FROM_LIST`, and changes to those fields are never applied as a full set.

blocks.item: **Incremental payloads with only `urls`:** in the `ADD_TO_LIST` / `REMOVE_FROM_LIST` payloads, send only `urls` (empty or omitted for the other list fields), then send a full update without an action for the remaining fields whenever any of them changed. Or simply always finish with a full update after the incremental calls.
**Incremental diffs for every list field:** compute add/remove sets for each list field, the same way it's done for `urls`.

blocks.text: Immediately after any apply that changes `urls` on a category with `db_categorized_urls` entries, run a second plan/apply. The category is wrong in ZIA in the time between the two applies.

`urls` has `DiffSuppressFunc: suppressURLCategoriesReorderDiff`, which compares `d.GetChange("urls")`. If the attribute is removed from config, or set to `null` (e.g. `urls = length(var.urls) > 0 ? var.urls : null`), `GetChange` returns the state value for both old and new. The function decides the lists are equal and suppresses the removal. **The last URL is never removed from ZIA, and the plan stays clean.** Passing `urls = []` explicitly makes the removal show up in the plan.
Two more observations on that function:

blocks.item: **The check:** it should probably consult `d.GetRawConfig()` (or treat a null config value as empty) rather than relying on `GetChange`.
**The cache:** `urlsReorderSuppressionCache` is a package-level `sync.Map` keyed by resource ID and never cleared, so the first result for an ID is reused for the rest of the provider process.
